newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: IMF sees no overheating in Philippine economy.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees no overheating in Philippine economy.

text.p: The Philippines is not showing signs of overheating and measures are in place to prevent any economic disruption, the International Monetary Fund's Manila resident representative David Nellor said on Monday.

"A careful examination indicates that the current economic and financial situation of the Philippines is fundamentally sound. The present Philippine economic recovery ... shows no signs of overheating due to broad-based wage or other cost pressures," Nellor said in a statement.
The statement came after the government announced a slowdown in the inflation rate to 4.6 percent last month, and a healthy public sector surplus of 4.8 billion pesos as of end-1996.
He said the Philippines was competitive with the real exchange rate and export earnings remaining strong.

Nellor lauded the Central Bank's recent decision to increase the banks' minimum capital and the lowering of the value of loans given to the property sector to 60 percent from 70 percent of the appraised value.

"These measures are prudent steps," he said, adding that the Central Bank had strengthened the financial sector to withstand any economic shock or cyclical development of a sector, particularly in the real estate industry.
